title: LETTER 5: Letter from Bank to Loan Defaulter — Recovery Notice

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: A loan recovery notice is a formal communication sent by a bank to a borrower defaulting on loan installments.
The letter must clearly mention account details, outstanding dues, overdue principal, interest accrued, and a firm deadline for payment.
Account default exceeding 90 days leads to classification as a Non-Performing Asset (NPA) under RBI guidelines.
Failure to clear dues within the specified timeline empowers the bank to initiate legal proceedings under the SARFAESI Act, 2002 or Debt Recovery Tribunals (DRT).
In descriptive writing exams, maintaining a professional, assertive, yet legally complaint tone is critical for scoring high marks.

blocks.content: Failure to clear the outstanding dues within 15 days will compel the bank to initiate legal proceedings under the SARFAESI Act, 2002 for recovery of the loan.

rows: Account classified as NPA (90+ days overdue)
Remind borrower and encourage voluntary settlement
Pre-requisite step before enforcing security interest/seizure

items: Always include mandatory elements: Loan Account Number, Total Overdue Amount, Specific Deadline Date, and Consequences of Non-Payment.
Ensure formal letter format: Sender Address (Bank Manager), Date, Receiver Address (Borrower), Subject Line, Salutation, Body, and Formal Sign-off.
Avoid informal or aggressive language; stick to official banking terminology and regulatory compliance language.
